record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the compressible Navier-Stokes equations for viscous polytropic flows with fixed positive viscosity and nonnegative heat conductivity and without exterior forcing, is the Cauchy problem or the initial-boundary-value problem globally well posed for large data? If singularities form in finite or infinite time, can vacuum appear even when the initial data are initially away from vacuum, what are the admissible function spaces for post-singularity weak solutions, and what is the large-time asymptotic behavior of those weak solutions?

evidence.quote: Global (in time) well-posedness of the Cauchy problem or initial-boundary value of problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with large data. Consider the Navier Stokes equations for viscous polytropic flows with fixed positive viscosity and nonnegative heat conductivity without exterior forcing.

Is there formation of singularities in finite time (or even in infinite time) for the solutions with large smooth data [39]? Can the vacuum state be formed in finite time even the data are given away from the vacuum? If there exist singularities forming from smooth solutions, can one characterize the structures of the singularity ... ? What are the appropriate spaces to study the weak solutions after formations of singularities? What are the large time asymptotic behavior of the weak solutions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the compressible Navier–Stokes equations governing a viscous polytropic gas in d=2 or 3 spatial dimensions, written for the density ρ(t,x) ≥ 0, the velocity u(t,x) ∈ R^d, and the absolute temperature θ(t,x) ≥ 0:

∂_t ρ + div(ρ u) = 0,
∂_t(ρ u) + div(ρ u ⊗ u) + ∇p = μ Δu + (μ+λ) ∇ div u,
∂_t(ρ E) + div((ρ E + p) u) = div(κ ∇θ) + div(S · u),

where E = e + |u|^2/2 with internal energy e = c_v θ, the pressure is given by the polytropic law p = R ρ θ (R, c_v > 0), the viscous stress is S = μ(∇u + ∇u^T) + λ div u · I with shear viscosity μ > 0 fixed and bulk viscosity satisfying 2μ + dλ ≥ 0, and the heat conductivity satisfies κ ≥ 0. No exterior force or heat source is applied. Equip the system with either (a) Cauchy data on R^d, or (b) physically admissible boundary conditions on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d.

Address the following questions for arbitrarily large initial data:

1. Is the Cauchy problem (and the initial–boundary-value problem) globally well posed in time for large initial data (without smallness assumptions)?

2. If singularities can form, can they form in finite or infinite time for solutions issuing from large but smooth, vacuum-free initial data (i.e., with inf ρ_0 > 0)? In particular, can the vacuum state {ρ = 0} appear in finite time from initial data that are bounded away from vacuum?

3. Identify the admissible function spaces in which weak solutions can be defined and studied after singularity formation, and characterize the structure of such singularities.

4. Determine the large-time asymptotic behavior of these weak solutions.

Provide proofs or counterexamples for each of (1)–(4).
artifact.status_search_result: Global well-posedness of the full compressible Navier–Stokes system in 2D/3D for large initial data, the possibility of finite-time vacuum formation from non-vacuum smooth data, the proper functional framework for weak solutions past singularities, and their long-time asymptotics remain widely recognized as major open problems. Recent surveys and research papers (e.g., works by Xin, Huang, Li, Feireisl, and others through the 2020s) report only partial results: blow-up criteria, finite-energy weak solutions à la Lions–Feireisl for the barotropic case, and conditional regularity, but no resolution in the large-data regime for the full polytropic system.

status_evidence.title: Blowup of smooth solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: Xin and Yan show finite-time blowup for classical solutions of the full compressible Navier–Stokes equations when the initial density has compact support, leaving the large-data global well-posedness question open.
status_evidence.claim: Global well-posedness for large smooth data remains open; blowup is known under vacuum-related conditions.

status_evidence.title: On the global well-posedness for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works continue to address only small-data or conditional regularity results for the full compressible Navier–Stokes system.
status_evidence.claim: Large-data global well-posedness for the full system is still unresolved.
